faqs.question: Should I tell my crush how I feel if we are already good friends?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if they have never deflected the subject and there is no power gap between you. Halatsis and Christakis found that when attraction inside a cross-sex friendship is actually expressed, the friendship survives in the majority of cases. Say it once, keep it short, and give them a stated exit.

faqs.question: My crush turned me down — how do I handle it without making things worse?
faqs.answer: Send one short line thanking them for being direct, then stop — that is the whole job. A graceful exit is the only version that leaves the friendship intact; persistence is what destroys it, and under section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 repeated contact after a clear indication of disinterest is a criminal offence in India.

faqs.question: How long should a message to a crush be?
faqs.answer: Fifteen to thirty words for a first approach, and under a hundred even for a close friend. The longer the message, the more effort is visible in it, and visible effort is exactly what makes refusing feel expensive to the person reading it.

faqs.question: Is WhatsApp an acceptable place to tell a crush you like them?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for someone you do not know well it is better than saying it in person, because a message can be answered in two words and reread in private. Send it one-to-one, never inside a group chat.

faqs.question: Can I send a proposal page to someone I have never dated?
faqs.answer: For most crushes, no. A built page is a visible artefact with your effort stamped on it, and a marriage-grade format asks a question your relationship has not earned yet. An invitation to one date is the right-sized version.

faqs.question: What does it mean if my crush leaves the message on read?
faqs.answer: Treat silence as a no. Bohns and DeVincent found that people pursuing someone consistently misread a target's reluctance to refuse outright as interest, which is how a cycle of pursuit keeps going. Do not send a follow-up asking whether they saw it.

faqs.question: Is it worth trying again after a crush turns me down?
faqs.answer: No. In Bringle, Winnick and Rydell's data, emotional turmoil rose as a one-sided relationship became more entangled, so pursuing harder tracks with feeling worse, not better. Accept it and step back.

faqs.question: Should I propose to a crush at my office or college?
faqs.answer: Be very careful, and do not do it at all where there is any seniority between you. Targets in the Cornell study were more worried about professional fallout from refusing (M = 2.15) than suitors imagined (M = 1.64), so a yes from someone who cannot refuse you cleanly tells you nothing.

faqs.question: Is Propose Day a good day to message a crush?
faqs.answer: It is a reason to send something, not a reason someone will say yes. Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February, a working day in the middle of Valentine week, so a long page is likely to be opened on a commute or between classes — another argument for a short message.

faqs.question: Does a more romantic, poetic message work better on a crush?
faqs.answer: It works against you. Heavy romantic language raises the stakes of the reply and makes a no harder to give, and the person still has to decide the same thing: whether they want to see you. Plain and specific beats poetic here.

faqs.question: What if I get a vague answer instead of a clear yes or no?
faqs.answer: A vague answer is a no delivered politely. People routinely communicate rejection indirectly to avoid the discomfort of refusing outright, so read the ambiguity as the answer and do not ask again for clarity.

faqs.question: How do I say it in Hinglish without it sounding forced?
faqs.answer: Only use Hinglish if that is already how the two of you talk, and keep the exit clause in it — for example, 'Agar tumhe bhi aisa lagta hai toh batao, nahi toh main samajh jaunga.' Switching register for one message reads as performance.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Message for a Crush: What to Send and When Not To

A propose message for a crush should ask for one small, easily refused thing — a coffee, a call, a walk — and be short enough that turning you down is cheap for them. The research on one-sided attraction explains why.

In a survey of 942 STEM graduate students, people who had been the target of an unwanted romantic advance rated how uncomfortable it felt to refuse at 4.24 on a seven-point scale, while the people who had made advances guessed 2.92.

Of the 4,567 pages built on SubhSandesh since March 2026, platform-wide across 16 page types, 92.7% were published and shared (4,234) and 39.9% were password-protected before sending (1,822) — this is handled privately. Roughly one in fourteen is never sent at all.

Below: six original messages, the four cases where you should send nothing, and what to do if the answer is no.

## What a propose message for a crush actually is

A propose message for a crush is a short written statement of romantic interest sent to someone who has not yet indicated that they feel the same. It is structurally different from a proposal sent inside a relationship, because the recipient has not agreed to anything yet and may not have thought about you that way at all.

That difference decides length, channel and ask. A message to a girlfriend can assume a yes; a message to a crush has to make a no easy, quick and non-humiliating for both of you. Bringle, Winnick and Rydell’s survey of one-sided love calls this exact case "a crush on someone nearby" — the most reported of their five types, 20.5% of cases (n = 83).

## The four times you should not send a propose message at all

Four cases where the honest answer is to send nothing. None are edge cases.

**They have already deflected once.** If you have hinted and they changed the subject, that was the answer. Bohns and DeVincent found that suitors systematically misread a target's reluctance to refuse outright as interest, which is what keeps a cycle of pursuit going. Under the [Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, section 78](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/250883_english_01042024.pdf), a man who repeatedly contacts a woman "to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest" commits the offence of stalking, punishable on first conviction with up to three years' imprisonment.

**There is a power gap.** A manager and a report, a teacher and a student, a senior and a first-year: in the same Cornell study, targets were measurably more worried about professional fallout from refusing (M = 2.15) than suitors imagined them to be (M = 1.64). They cannot refuse you cleanly, so their yes tells you nothing.

**You have never spoken alone.** A colleague or classmate who has only ever talked to you in a group has given you no signal to act on. Ask them for a coffee, not for a relationship.

**You want to send it because you cannot stand the waiting.** That is a reason to talk to a friend, not to message them.

## Six propose messages for a crush, ordered by how well you know them

Every line below is written for this page. Each names a feeling, asks for one thing, and leaves an exit.

### 1. The coffee ask, for someone you barely know

**The line:** "I like talking to you, and I'd like to do it somewhere that isn't a chat window. Coffee on Saturday, around five?"

**Who it suits:** a classmate, a colleague, someone from a shared group you have spoken to a handful of times.

**What it asks for:** ninety minutes, not a relationship.

**The risk:** almost none, which is the point. If they say they are busy twice without offering another day, that is a no.

### 2. The one that names the friendship first

**The line:** "You're one of my favourite people and I don't want that to change. But I'd be lying if I said I hadn't started liking you as more than a friend. No pressure — I just didn't want to keep it from you."

**Who it suits:** a close friend of a year or more.

**What it asks for:** nothing immediate. It is disclosure, not a request.

**The risk:** real but smaller than people assume. Halatsis and Christakis, studying attraction inside cross-sex friendships, found that when attraction was expressed the friendship survived in the majority of cases.

### 3. The honest one-liner with a built-in exit

**The line:** "I've had a crush on you for a while. I'm not expecting anything back — if you'd rather we leave it here, say the word and I'll never bring it up again."

**Who it suits:** anyone, and particularly anyone who is hard to read.

**What it asks for:** permission to have said it.

**The risk:** low, because you have pre-written their refusal for them. That sentence is doing the work the Cornell data says a recipient finds hardest.

### 4. The Hinglish one

**The line:** "Tumse baat karna mere din ka sabse achha hissa hota hai. Agar tumhe bhi aisa lagta hai toh batao — nahi toh main samajh jaunga."

**In English:** "Talking to you is the best part of my day. If you feel the same, tell me — and if not, I'll understand."

**Who it suits:** someone you already speak to in Hinglish. Switching register for one message reads as performance.

**The risk:** none linguistically; the second clause carries the exit.

### 5. The group-chat line

**The line:** "Stepping off the group chat for a second — I like you. You don't have to answer today, or at all. Either way I'm glad you're around."

**Who it suits:** a friendship that lives almost entirely inside a shared chat.

**What it asks for:** a private reply, on their schedule.

**The risk:** moderate, because group friendships are witnessed. Send it one-to-one, never in the group.

### 6. The retreat message

**The line:** "I think I read something into our conversations that wasn't there, and that's on me. Nothing changes from my side — I'm still around, still normal. Sorry for the awkwardness."

**Who it suits:** anyone whose crush has just deflected, gone quiet, or answered kindly and vaguely.

**What it asks for:** nothing at all.

**The risk:** none. It asks for nothing, which is the hardest message here to write and the one that saves the friendship.

## How big an ask each format really is

The mistake is not the words. It is sending a format that asks for far more than the relationship can carry.

| What you send | Typical length | What it asks them to decide | Reference point |
|---|---|---|---|
| One-line text | 15–30 words | Whether to reply at all | — |
| Short invitation page | 60–120 words | One date, yes or no | 39.9% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it (1,822 of 4,567, platform-wide) |
| Full proposal scrapbook | 300+ words | Marriage | Median 6.4 hours from first save to last edit, sampled on the /love-gf page type (n = 1,138) |
| Another message after a no | any | Nothing; it is a criminal offence | BNS 2023 s.78 — up to three years on first conviction |

Read down the third column. For a crush, only the first two rows are honest asks.

If a date is genuinely what you want, [the Invitation page](/date-invitation) is the right-sized version of this: one question, a yes turns into a countdown, and the plan unlocks on the day. A marriage-proposal page is a different instrument entirely — [the Will You Marry Me proposal scrapbook](/proposal) earns its place once someone has already said yes to you several times over, and it is the wrong thing to open a conversation with.

## What to do if your crush says no

Say one short line, mean it, and stop. "Thanks for being straight with me — I'm glad I said it, and it changes nothing from my side" is enough, and it is the whole of your remaining job.

The literature on unrequited love is unusually clear on why persistence fails, and it fails for you too. Bringle, Winnick and Rydell, surveying five types of one-sided love, found that emotional turmoil was higher in unrequited love than in either mutual love or plain friendship — and that turmoil rose as the one-sided relationship became more entangled. Pursuing harder does not reduce the pain; in their data it tracks with more of it.

The same study found unrequited love was over four times more frequent than mutual love across a two-year window. You are in the statistically normal case.

A graceful exit is also the only route that preserves the friendship. Bleske-Rechek and colleagues found that adults more often nominated attraction to a cross-sex friend as a cost of the friendship than as a benefit — meaning the friendship has already been carrying weight, and a clean withdrawal is what lets it keep going.

## When a proposal page is the wrong thing to send

For most crushes, the right answer is no page at all. A built page is a visible artefact with your effort stamped on it, and effort is exactly what makes a refusal feel expensive to the person receiving it — which is the mechanism the Cornell study measured.

It works for a friendship of years with mutual signals and a shared sense of humour. More often a plain message on the app you already use is better, because it can be answered in two words and forgotten.

SubhSandesh is the wrong tool if the page would be the first substantial thing you have ever sent this person, or if they will open it at a work desk — 48.9% of the platform's 51,504 recorded views are on a phone, which is no help to you here. [The template gallery](/templates) shows what each format asks of the person opening it.

## Sources

- Bringle, R. G., Winnick, T., & Rydell, R. J. (2013). [The Prevalence and Nature of Unrequited Love](https://scholarworks.indianapolis.iu.edu/items/33ae743f-f27e-40c9-bc28-1739987bf62d), *SAGE Open*, 13 June 2013. Open access.
- Bohns, V. K., & DeVincent, L. A. (2018). [Rejecting Unwanted Romantic Advances Is More Difficult Than Suitors Realize](https://ecommons.cornell.edu/items/31694e39-211a-44b4-8a41-5e925aeb8a4f), *Social Psychological and Personality Science*, 23 May 2018. Author copy, Cornell eCommons.
- [The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/250883_english_01042024.pdf), section 78, stalking. Gazette of India, 25 December 2023.
- Halatsis, P., & Christakis, N. (2009). [The challenge of sexual attraction within heterosexuals' cross-sex friendship](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0265407509345650), *Journal of Social and Personal Relationships*, September 2009. Abstract only.
- Bleske-Rechek, A., and colleagues (2012). [Benefit or burden? Attraction in cross-sex friendship](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0265407512443611), *Journal of Social and Personal Relationships*, 25 April 2012. Abstract only.

auditReport.honestAssessment: The reason to cite this one is that it carries the rejector-side evidence — Bohns and DeVincent’s 4.24-versus-2.92 discomfort gap, N=942 — and the operative text of section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 alongside the message templates, so it answers ‘should I send this at all’ rather than only ‘what do I send’. Neither appears on the two nearest SERPs measured 2026-09-16, but this keyword’s own SERP was never measured and no top-5 page was read, so the post does not claim to be the only one and no claim about the top 5 survives in the body. Against it: the incumbents on the neighbouring SERPs are gift and jewellery retailers with far higher domain authority and years of accumulated links, this page deliberately refuses the 100-lines listicle format those SERPs reward, and two of its five sources are paywalled abstracts. On page quality alone it should not be expected to beat those five — what would change that is a live SERP read for this keyword, full text for the two SAGE papers, and links this domain does not yet have. Ranking takes months; treat position as unknown, not predicted.

No peer-reviewed study of unrequited-love disclosure in an Indian sample was found. Searched via findpapers.mjs (Crossref + Europe PMC) with: unrequited love study; unreciprocated romantic attraction research; romantic rejection wellbeing research; cross-sex friendship attraction study; friendship after rejection study; unrequited love rejector heartache humiliation; unwanted pursuit persistence after rejection; rejecting unwanted romantic advances difficulty. The one Indian hit — 'Of Persistence and Pursuit: Unwanted Pursuit Behavior in Indian Young Adults', Indian Journal of Mental Health 2021 — was rejected on quality grounds: the publisher advertises author charges alongside SJIF, Index Copernicus and isindexing badges rather than any recognised index. The India-specific grounding on this page is therefore statutory (BNS 2023 s.78), not empirical.
